subject: Mathematics
overall_notes: Strong capstone closer. ALIGNMENT (4): C4 integrated and the expanded_walkthrough explicitly bridges Lessons 1-4 ('ASK math questions (L1), COLLECT data (L2), PREDICT from data (L3), REFLECT/REFINE (L4)'). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH (4): the data-as-decoration trap is named with Lehrer & Schauble 2002 citation, and recovery_moves branch by diagnostic (A: PREDICT disconnected, B: cites but doesn't extend, C: skips REFINE) — substitute-actionable. INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE (4): all materials are everyday (templates, situation cards, anchor charts), and the differentiation includes an explicit NO-PAPER VERSION (5-fold sheet OR oral capstone). 12/25/13 = 50 min is realistic for G2. CLARITY_VOICE (4): the closing refrain 'Math lives in our town — and WE are the math!' is a memorable quotable chant used in both hook and exit_routine; success criteria all 'I can'; vocabulary reinforced child-friendly. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY (4): Lehrer & Schauble cited by name, children invent/refine their own model and compare via gallery walk, modelling cycle anchors data-to-prediction grounding rather than treating data as decoration. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY (4): 5 worksheet parts mirror 5-step cycle, AND Part 6 'Modeller's Switch' is a deliberate transfer probe (unfamiliar trees-not-buses situation, 12 + 3×4 = 24) explicitly justified in teacher_notes as verifying generalization beyond rehearsed scenarios.
